WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, and it is a finding rather than a convenience.
PaymentTypeLabelTest::test_every_old_map_key_still_resolves read the map out of git history
directly. CI checks out with actions/checkout@v4 and NO fetch-depth, so the clone is depth 1
while this commit is 347 behind HEAD -- `git show c7283a3c~1:...` fails, the test took its
"history unavailable" branch, and asserted assertTrue(true). So the DERIVED half of that
ratchet -- the half written because "a hand copy is exactly what let DPO through" -- had never
executed on a runner. Only the hand-written list beside it ever ran, which is the exact thing
Proved with a real shallow clone rather than deduced: `git clone --depth 1` reports 1 cloned
commit, and `git show c7283a3c~1:...` answers "fatal: invalid object name".
THE TEST STILL CROSS-CHECKS THIS AGAINST GIT wherever the history IS readable, so the fixture
cannot drift from the truth on any machine that can see the truth. What changed is that the
derived assertion now runs everywhere, instead of only where somebody has a full clone.
